articleTitle: The application of the geometrical theory of diffraction to modelling pulsed ultrasonic inspection: a system model
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Mathematical Modelling for NDT
abstract: Summary form only given. A theoretical model for pulsed ultrasonic inspection is described. A particularly attractive element of the model is that it predicts the pulse shape at the receiving transducer, based on the knowledge of the pulse shape scattered from some suitable reference reflector. The model is a development of that described by Chapman and Coffey (see CEGB Report No.NW/SSD/82/0034/R, 1982), and uses the earlier formulation to take account of the geometries of the flaw and test piece, the modelling of the transmitted probe beam, the geometry of the probe scan, the interaction of the incident field with the flaw to produce the scattered field, and the interaction of the scattered field with the receiving probe. Thus the model can properly be termed an integrated 'system' model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calculation of diffraction coefficients for ultrasonic interactions at a right-angled corner
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Mathematical Modelling for NDT
abstract: Summary form only given. A partial model has been developed for calculating the far-field effects of the interaction of an ultrasonic pulse with a flaw. This model uses finite differences to calculate the displacements on the flaw surface, and then an integral formulation to obtain the signals at any other point. Comparisons have been made with the results of calculations using other methods (simple finite difference, Kirchhoff approximation, geometrical theory of diffraction) in conditions where they are known to be valid and excellent agreement obtained. The model has also been used to obtain diffraction coefficients for the scattering of an ultrasonic pulse from a right-angled corner. This is a canonical problem in elastic theory, and also forms the basis for the calculation of the scattering from a flat-bottomed hole, often used as a calibration reflector. Comparisons have been made with measurements, both for compression waves and shear waves, and good agreement obtained in amplitude and phase.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Elastic wave propagation and scattering in inhomogeneous and anisotropic materials
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Mathematical Modelling for NDT
abstract: Summary form only given. Finite difference models for calculations of pulsed wave propagation have been created for problems involving either two or three spatial dimensions. Time dependent solutions are calculated for a short duration pulse of a finite width beam in a material with arbitrary inhomogeneity and anisotropy within the calculational region. The results are displayed as A-scans at particular detector positions, as contour plots of compression and shear wave energies, as Poynting vectors, or as differential scattering cross-sections, and may be compared with experimental measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A model for the ultrasonic inspection of rough defects
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Mathematical Modelling for NDT
abstract: Summary form only given. A model, based on acoustic Kirchhoff theory, capable of simulating many aspects of rough defect inspection, was developed. The principles of this model are presented, together with predictions from the model and comparison with experiments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Finite difference modelling of echo responses
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Mathematical Modelling for NDT
abstract: Echo responses from targets interrogated by realistic transducer signals are calculated. The case of a circular transducer on the surface of a half-(3-)space is discussed. The problem is modelled using a finite difference grid.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scattering of elastic waves from surface indentations
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Mathematical Modelling for NDT
abstract: The study originates from a project designed to look into ways of detecting pitting corrosion on the remote side of thick aluminium plates. Corrosion pits are genuinely three-dimensional objects and can be represented as hemispherical surface indentations in a stress free plane surface. The incident field generated by an ultrasonic transducer is assumed to be a time harmonic plane wave, and the different wave components scattered by a surface disturbance provide information on the location and size of the corrosion pit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of focused ultrasonic transducers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Mathematical Modelling for NDT
abstract: Shows how theoretical results obtained from computer modelling can be presented in such a way as to provide a clear and practically relevant guidelines for the design of focused ultrasonic transducers. The results are applicable to sound beams produced either from disc-shaped transducers focused by means of axicon, toroidal or spherical lenses or from similarly shaped piezoelectric elements. Because the results have been extracted directly from a realistic computer modelling procedure, they do not suffer from the inaccuracies incurred when approximate analytical formulae are derived.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calculation of the response of electromagnetic acoustic transducers to broadband acoustic transients
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Mathematical Modelling for NDT
abstract: Summary form only given. Electromagnetic acoustic transducers (EMATs) operate via a Lorentz force interaction between an acoustic wave and a static magnetic field. This generates eddy currents which can be detected by a suitably orientated coil. A Nd:YAG laser with a risetime of 10 mu s is used to generate line or point ultrasonic sources with normal drive and approximately Heaviside time dependence. Solutions for these ultrasonic sources give the surface displacement. In order to calculate the response of the EMATs to these displacements, the authors convolve with an appropriate time function and differentiate to give velocity. This is easiest on epicentre (on the opposite face vertically below the source) where the waves approximate to plane waves and phase differences across the face of the EMAT can be ignored. The waveform can be calculated by convolving with a Gaussian time function appropriate to the band width of the EMAT/amplifier combination.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
